title: SC-MT014-HandshakePrimitivesToolSurface

scope.summary:
GOAL: Build the Handshake Primitives Tool Surface - ONE uniform registry through which Handshake exposes its own API/primitives as tools to EVERY agent session, on every lane, vendor-agnostically. OPERATOR FRAMING (2026-07-22): exposing Handshake primitives to models is a core engine capability of the wrapper. Without this MT, each tool family ships its own bespoke MCP server (MM MT-101/102 spawn+steer tools, AC MT-206 annotation tools), which fragments discovery, policy, and attribution, and makes adding the next primitive (or the next vendor lane) an N-by-M problem. This MT delivers the shared foundation those register into: define a primitive once, and Claude, GPT/Codex, ACP, and future lanes all get it - governed identically.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New module src/backend/handshake_core/src/agent_sessions/primitives_surface.rs: PrimitiveToolDef { tool_id (stable, kebab), version, description (model-facing), input_schema (JSON Schema), tool_class (maps into MT-011 ToolClass::HandshakePrimitive subtypes), handler (async trait object), provenance_stamping (bool, default true), rate_limit }; a PrimitiveToolRegistry (in-process registration at boot; families register their defs); ONE session-facing tool server built on the mcp/gate.rs server-side pattern serving the registry over the session tool channel; per-lane exposure adapters (Claude lane: tools appear via the session MCP config; Codex lane: MCP server config; ACP lane: MCP capability passthrough) - all three reuse the SAME server, only the wiring differs.

GOVERNANCE PIPELINE (uniform, in order, for every call): (1) session identity resolved server-side (session_id, parent, role) - never model-supplied; (2) MT-011 SessionToolGate evaluation (tool_class HandshakePrimitive rules + role tool_policy from RO MT-081); (3) SC MT-012 ToolCallRequested hooks; (4) input schema validation (reject malformed with typed error the model can read); (5) handler execution with rate limits; (6) provenance stamping (robot_id/session_id/run_id) on any write primitive; (7) ledger row + FR event (RD MT-161) per call. V1 REGISTERED PRIMITIVES (delivered by their owning MTs, registered here): spawn_worker/steer_worker/interrupt_worker/worker_status/list_children (MM MT-101/102), annotation_create/annotation_list/annotation_reply (AC MT-206), plus two delivered IN this MT as reference implementations: session_info (read own session/thread/turn state, capabilities, workspace binding) and mt_status (read the dispatched MT run state from ML MT-123 for the session's own wp/mt scope).

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read mcp/gate.rs (GatedMcpClient + server patterns), MM MT-101/102 and AC MT-206 contracts (their tool schemas become registry entries), MT-011 (gate), MT-012 (hooks).
2. Define PrimitiveToolDef/Registry types; registration API with duplicate-id rejection and version metadata; registry snapshot exposed for diagnostics (RD MT-166 join).
3. Build the shared tool server on the mcp server-side pattern: list_tools from the registry (filtered by what the SESSION'S ROLE may see - a model must not even discover tools its policy denies, discovery-filtering per role tool_policy), call_tool through the 7-step governance pipeline.
4. Implement the two reference primitives (session_info, mt_status) end to end incl. schemas, handlers, tests.
5. Wire per-lane exposure: Claude interactive preset gains the Handshake MCP server in its session MCP config; Codex app-server/exec lanes reference the same server; ACP lane advertises it via MCP capability passthrough. No lane-specific tool logic anywhere.
6. Migrate-by-registration: MM/AC tool families register into this registry (their MTs keep their handlers; this MT provides the registration seam and asserts via test that bespoke parallel servers are not admitted - one server, many primitives).
7. Tests: discovery filtering by role, full governance pipeline order (gate deny blocks before handler, hook deny blocks, schema reject typed), provenance auto-stamping, rate limits, identical tool list served across two lanes (fake adapter + one real lane or typed blocker).
forbidden_paths: src/frontend/** (no GUI; registry snapshot surfaces via RD MT-166)
acceptance_criteria: PrimitiveToolRegistry with stable tool_ids, versions, JSON-Schema inputs, duplicate rejection; registry snapshot queryable.
One shared tool server serves the registry to sessions; discovery is role-filtered (a denied tool is invisible, not just refused - proven by test).

Every call runs the full pipeline in order: identity -> MT-011 gate -> MT-012 hooks -> schema validation -> handler -> provenance stamp -> ledger+FR; each stage's rejection is typed and model-readable; order proven by test.
session_info and mt_status reference primitives work end to end with tests.
MM and AC tool families register into this registry; a test asserts no bespoke parallel tool server is admitted for primitives.
The identical tool list is served on two different lanes from the same registry (fake adapter + one real lane, or typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF).
Provenance (robot_id/session_id/run_id) is stamped server-side on write primitives and cannot be supplied by the model.
No vendor names in registry types, tool ids, or schemas.
proof_targets: cargo test -p handshake_core primitives_surface --nocapture 2>&1 | grep -E 'test result: ok'
expected_tests: pipeline order + typed rejections per stage
implementation_notes: OPERATOR FRAMING 2026-07-22: Handshake API/primitives exposure is an engine capability; the wrapper defines the tool surface once, lanes only differ in wiring. This is also the seam future Handshake-built projects inherit.

MM MT-101/102 and AC MT-206 predate this MT in authoring order; at activation, packet-level ordering runs MT-014 in the same phase so their handlers register here instead of standing up bespoke servers (their contracts already follow the gate.rs pattern, so registration is a thin adaptation - record it in their implementation sessions, do not rewrite their contracts).
Discovery filtering matters for prompt-injection surface reduction: an invisible tool cannot be socially engineered into use.

MCP is the carrier because all current lanes speak it (verified 2026-07-21 research: Claude session MCP config, Codex MCP tool support, ACP reuses MCP types); the registry itself is transport-neutral - a future non-MCP lane implements the same exposure trait.
mt_status reads ML MT-123 run state scoped to the session's own dispatch - a worker may see its own MT state, never the whole board (scope rule in handler).

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend registry + server; registry snapshot and per-call audit surface via RD MT-166.

target_entries: Dexterity primitives tool surface: what tools sessions get, how discovery/policy filtering works
Registering a new Handshake primitive (for future feature MTs)

risk_if_missed: Primitive exposure stays N-by-M (each tool family x each vendor lane), discovery/policy/attribution fragment across bespoke servers, and adding the next vendor or the next primitive multiplies work instead of registering once.

risks: RISK-1: A primitive handler bypasses the gate/hook pipeline (direct registration of an ungoverned tool).
RISK-2: Model-supplied provenance spoofs attribution on write primitives.
RISK-3: Tool discovery leaks denied tools, inviting prompt-injection attempts against them.
RISK-4: mt_status/session_info leak cross-session state (a worker reads the whole board or another session's data).
RISK-5: Bespoke parallel tool servers reappear, re-fragmenting governance.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): The server is the only call path; handlers are invoked exclusively by the pipeline; pipeline-order test mandatory.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Provenance fields are stamped server-side from session identity; model-supplied values rejected with typed error; tested.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Role-filtered discovery - denied tools are absent from list_tools; tested.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Reference primitives enforce own-session/own-dispatch scope in handlers; cross-scope test proves denial.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Admission test asserts primitives are served only via the registry server; code review gate for new tool servers.

research_provenance.source: Operator vendor-agnostic-engine directive 2026-07-22 (Handshake API/primitives exposure is an engine capability); mcp/gate.rs incumbent pattern; MM MT-101/102 + AC MT-206 tool schemas as first registrants; 2026-07-21 research pass (MCP support across Claude/Codex/ACP lanes).
